subject: Walkman Court Redevelopment and Contractor Wage Concerns
overview: The Board of Commissioners discussed the ongoing redevelopment and resident relocation efforts at Walkman Court and approved a new action plan for the Family Self-Sufficiency program. The board tabled a procurement resolution following concerns regarding a contractor's history of wage violations.

items.title: Minutes
items.summary: The board approved minutes from the regular meeting and executive session held on August 17, 2022.

items.title: Financial Statements
items.summary: The board accepted the July financial statements, which showed the agency adding $2.3 million to its reserves and operating within budget despite REAC inspection costs.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The board voted to enter executive session to discuss pending litigation and contract negotiations.

items.title: Executive Director's Report
items.summary: Jeffrey Driscoll addressed the professional tenor of board meetings before providing updates on Walkman Court renovations, zoning negotiations with the Department of Transportation, and resident relocation progress.

items.title: Resolution 53 of 2022
items.summary: The board tabled a resolution regarding contractor selection after a commissioner presented reports that the low-bid vendor had recently paid nearly $300,000 in penalties for wage and overtime violations.

items.title: Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) Action Plan
items.summary: Sandra Reiniger presented an overview of the FSS program and its escrow account incentives; the board subsequently approved the updated FSS Action Plan required by HUD.

items.title: Routine Business and Meeting Schedule
items.summary: The board rescheduled the October meeting to October 20 and received an update on a preliminary Community Preservation Act funding application for Walkman Court.
